editorial:
Imagine the worst nightmare any parent could face: your child vanishes without a trace. You follow Daniel, a father who refuses to give up hope after his teenage son disappears. Most of the story takes place around the Vistula River, where Daniel spends his days searching the water. The vibe is heavy and sad, but it feels very real because it focuses on that gut-wrenching feeling of not knowing the truth. You really feel for Daniel as he swings between thinking his son is gone and believing he might still be out there somewhere.

What really works here is how the director captures the loneliness of the search. The pacing is slow, which matches the feeling of waiting for news that never comes. While it might feel too sad for some, the raw emotion makes it feel honest. If you can handle a real tear-jerker, you should definitely check this out. It is the kind of film that stays with you long after the credits roll.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Daniel finally finds the evidence he was looking for at the bottom of the river. He discovers his son's body, which confirms that the boy did not run away but actually died. While it is a heartbreaking discovery, it gives Daniel the answer he needed. The movie ends with him finally being able to grieve and start the process of moving on now that the mystery is over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful true stories and deep character studies.
